report.answer: Middleware composition is implemented in src/compose.ts, which exports a koa-compose-style `compose()` function that turns an array of [handler, params] tuples into a single async dispatcher with onion-style next()/dispatch(i+1) recursion, error handling via onError, and 404 fallback via onNotFound. It's invoked from src/hono-base.ts in the private `#dispatch` method (~line 451): the router's matchResult is passed to `compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)`, with a fast-path optimization at line 430-434 that skips compose entirely when only one handler matched.

Single-handler routes bypass compose() as a perf optimization

report.answer: Errors propagate on two nested levels. Inside src/compose.ts, each middleware call is wrapped in try/catch inside dispatch(i): if the thrown value is an Error and an onError handler was passed to compose(), it sets context.error and calls onError(err, context) to produce a response inline (isError=true), otherwise it rethrows up the call stack; app.onError() (hono-base.ts:271) sets this.errorHandler, which is what's passed as compose()'s onError argument at hono-base.ts line ~451. Outside compose, #dispatch wraps `await composed(c)` in its own try/catch and any escaping error (including compose's rethrown non-Error values or errors thrown before/after composition) is caught by #handleError (hono-base.ts:399-404), which calls this.errorHandler if it's an Error instance or rethrows otherwise; the single-handler fast path (matchResult[0].length===1) has an identical parallel try/catch/.catch() calling #handleError directly, bypassing compose entirely. The default errorHandler (lines 35-41) unwraps HTTPException-like errors via `getResponse()` or falls back to a generic 500 text response.

report.answer: Errors propagate on two nested levels. Inside src/compose.ts, each middleware call is wrapped in try/catch inside dispatch(i): if the thrown value is an Error and an onError handler was passed to compose(), it sets context.error and calls onError(err, context) to produce a response inline (isError=true), otherwise it rethrows up the call stack; app.onError() (hono-base.ts:271) sets this.errorHandler, which is what's passed as compose()'s onError argument at hono-base.ts line ~451. Outside compose, #dispatch wraps `await composed(c)` in its own try/catch and any escaping error (including compose's rethrown non-Error values or errors thrown before/after composition) is caught by #handleError (hono-base.ts:399-404), which calls this.errorHandler if it's an Error instance or rethrows otherwise; the single-handler fast path (matchResult[0].length===1) has an identical parallel try/catch/.catch() calling #handleError directly, bypassing compose entirely. The default errorHandler (lines 35-41) unwraps HTTPException-like errors via `getResponse()` or falls back to a generic 500 text response.

verified.summary: this.errorHandler is passed as compose()'s onError arg
outer #dispatch wraps composed(c) in try/catch and delegates to #handleError on any escape (e.g. non-finalized-context error, or rethrown non-Error)
#handleError only calls errorHandler for Error instances, else rethrows (so non-Error throws propagate out of fetch())
single-handler fast path duplicates the same try/catch + .catch(err => #handleError) pattern, skipping compose()
default errorHandler unwraps HTTPException via err.getResponse(), else logs and returns generic 500
